A1.justification: Both PDFs describe XDen-1K and retain identifiable corresponding methods, experiments, equations, and figures. All 10 pages of v1 and 19 pages of v2 were readable, with equations and visual results checked against rendered pages. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original CT-based reconstruction errors, synthetic and real volumetric-segmentation IoU results, and real-robot pick, place, and push demonstrations.

after.justification: v2 retains original segmentation and robot demonstrations and reports additional reconstruction analyses, physical-property prediction comparisons, and quantitative grasping results.

M1.justification: v2 Sec. 5.3 introduces an AnyGrasp adaptation that selects candidate grasps whose gripper endpoints are closest to the predicted center of mass. The core attenuation optimization and X-Field architecture remain unchanged. The additional X-Field equations express FiLM conditioning, density prediction, and loss operations already described in v1.

E1.justification: v2 adds explicit physical-property inference benchmarking, including total-mass and center-of-mass prediction, on XDen-1K in Sec. 5.1. Real-object reconstruction, PartNeXt-based synthetic training, volumetric segmentation, and robot manipulation remain covered. The category count changes from 148 to 137, but the PDFs do not establish whether this reflects changed object membership or recategorization.

E2.justification: The PartField comparison is retained. v2 additionally evaluates NeRF2Physics, GaussianProperty, and Pixie in Table 4; vanilla AnyGrasp and NeRF2Physics-guided AnyGrasp against reconstruction-derived CoM guidance in Table 6; and X-Field versus manual segmentation priors in Table 2. These are substantive additions to evaluated comparator sets, not merely new citations.

E3.justification: v1's 15-object CT MAPE evaluation, stratified by metal content, is replaced by five example rows reporting CT MAE and biplanar reprojection MAE/correlation; only four rows contain CT errors. v2 also introduces density MAE, CoM L1 distance, total-mass MAPE, grasp-success rate, and joint-torque evaluation. These changed and added protocols preclude interpreting the replacement CT values as same-setting improvements.

E4.justification: v2 adds comparisons of predicted versus manual segmentation priors and background noise, plus an analysis of removing manually modeled interior geometry (Sec. 4.2, Tables 2–3). These examine reconstruction dependence on prior quality. The earlier quantitative metal/non-metal grouping disappears. The interior-prior analysis is clearly introduced, although Table 3's 'Fine' columns are insufficiently defined.

E5.justification: v2 Table 2 introduces standard deviations alongside mean LAT/PA reprojection errors, whereas v1 reports point estimates and category means without dispersion. Neither version specifies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new standard deviations do not establish that additional experimental runs occurred.

E6.justification: The CT MAPE results are replaced, and substantial new results appear in v2 Tables 2–4 and 6. Table 4 reports NeRF2Physics best on density MAE and CoM distance, while Pixie has the lowest mass MAPE. Table 6 reports grasp success of 27.50%, 55.00%, and 77.75% for vanilla AnyGrasp, NeRF2Physics CoM, and reconstruction-derived CoM respectively. Segmentation IoUs remain exactly unchanged: PartField 53.185/38.410 and X-Field 72.645/49.251 on synthetic/real data.

T1.justification: The Beer–Lambert model, LAC-to-density approximation, homogeneous-region assumption, forward projection, and optimization equations are retained. v2's additional X-Field equations restate operations and losses already described in v1; they introduce no new theoretical result, substantive derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The central claims about a real-world density-field dataset and reconstruction from biplanar X-rays remain. v2 explicitly adds physical-reasoning benchmarking as a third application and refines the broad claim of improved embodied-AI accuracy into a specific claim about CoM-guided robotic grasping.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands the applicability qualifications: CT is treated as a partial reference, with low-voltage and metallic-component departures from the density model discussed; manual interior modeling is identified as a scalability limitation; and X-Field is distinguished from the manual priors used for dataset construction because its reprojection errors remain higher. It also discusses automation and sim-to-real improvements. v1's explicit conclusion caveat about imperfect X-ray pose alignment is removed.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents manual interior-geometry modeling, identifies geometry/segmentation resources, and adds a Hugging Face dataset-access link. Conversely, v1's synthetic-data recipe—7.6K objects, SDF-based partitioning, VLM material assignment, physical-property mapping, and simulated X-ray rendering—is largely removed, as is the explicit 20-CT-scan count. Acquisition hardware and exposure settings are retained. These are documentation changes, not proof that the underlying training collection changed.

R1.justification: The part-understanding discussion is expanded to distinguish 2D-to-3D fusion, native 3D methods, Gaussian representations, and radiance fields, with corresponding citation additions and removals. PuGS and implementation-related references are added. The central positioning against synthetic or inferred physical-property datasets remains, and several newly evaluated methods were already cited in v1.

P1.justification: v2 separates reconstruction methodology from the dataset section and substantially rewrites the abstract, contributions, dataset evaluation, part-understanding discussion, and conclusion. X-Field explanations are expanded, the dedicated synthetic-data subsection disappears, robot demonstrations are condensed, and acknowledgements and an additional affiliation are introduced.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column to a single-column layout. The statistics graphic is rearranged, the object gallery is replaced with curated-geometry examples, and the segmentation figure gains ground-truth examples while its IoU table becomes separate Table 5. Reconstruction tables are replaced and new benchmark/grasping tables added. Several original diagrams and robot images are retained but resized or relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 better supports the dataset's practical value through explicit physical-property benchmarks and quantitative grasping comparisons, where v1 offered only qualitative robot demonstrations. Reprojection analyses and clearer disclosure of manual priors also improve assessment of dataset fidelity. These gains are tempered by reduced CT-result reporting, removal of the synthetic-data recipe, and insufficient specification of new experimental sample sizes, trial counts, and refinement settings.
